deal_breakers.title: Asymmetric Termination Rights
deal_breakers.claim: The Provider has more favorable termination rights compared to the Customer, allowing for termination for convenience with shorter notice.
deal_breakers.plain_english: The Provider can end the contract quickly, while the Customer has to wait longer and give more notice, which is unfair.
deal_breakers.why_flagged: This imbalance could leave the Customer vulnerable if the Provider decides to terminate the agreement unexpectedly.
deal_breakers.suggested_negotiation: Change the termination notice period for the Customer to match the Provider's 15 days.

clause_balance.provider_terms: Can terminate for convenience with 15 days' notice.
clause_balance.customer_terms: Can only terminate for convenience after 12 months with 60 days' notice.
clause_balance.asymmetry_summary: The Provider has a significantly shorter notice period for termination compared to the Customer.

evidence.quote: Provider may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 15 days’ written notice to Customer.
Customer may terminate for convenience only after the first 12 months of the Term and upon 60 days’ written notice.

watch_out.title: Aggregate Liability Cap Analysis
watch_out.claim: The aggregate liability cap is limited to the fees paid or payable by the Customer during the three months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
watch_out.plain_english: If something goes wrong, the most you can get back is what you paid for the last three months, which might not be enough to cover your losses.
watch_out.why_flagged: This clause could leave the Customer vulnerable to significant financial losses without adequate recourse.
watch_out.suggested_negotiation: Change the liability cap to cover at least six months of fees or a percentage of total fees paid during the contract term.

evidence.quote: EXCEPT FOR CUSTOMER’S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY’S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO PROVIDER DURING THE THREE MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.

watch_out.title: Automatic Renewal Clause
watch_out.claim: The contract automatically renews unless the Customer provides a non-renewal notice at least 90 days before expiration.
watch_out.plain_english: The contract will keep renewing automatically unless you tell them not to at least 90 days in advance.
watch_out.why_flagged: This could lead to the Customer being stuck in a contract longer than intended if they miss the notice deadline.
watch_out.suggested_negotiation: Change the notice period for non-renewal to 30 days instead of 90 days.

clause_balance.customer_terms: The Customer must provide a 90-day notice to avoid automatic renewal.
clause_balance.asymmetry_summary: The Customer has a longer obligation to notify for non-renewal compared to the Provider's rights.

evidence.quote: Unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before expiration, the Agreement will automatically renew for successive 12-month periods.

watch_out.title: Data Retention After Deletion
watch_out.claim: Provider may retain backup copies of Customer Data for up to 180 days after deletion from production systems.
watch_out.plain_english: The Provider can keep your data backups for up to 180 days after you delete them, which could be risky.
watch_out.why_flagged: This retention period could expose the Customer to risks if data is not adequately protected during this time.
watch_out.suggested_negotiation: Limit the retention period of backup copies to 30 days after deletion from production systems.

clause_balance.provider_terms: The Provider can retain backups for 180 days.
clause_balance.customer_terms: The Customer does not have control over the retention period of backups.
clause_balance.asymmetry_summary: The Provider has significant rights to retain data without the Customer's control.

evidence.quote: Provider may retain backup copies of Customer Data for up to 180 days after deletion from production systems, provided such copies remain protected and are not restored except for disaster recovery purposes.

watch_out.title: Indemnification Obligations
watch_out.claim: The Customer is obligated to defend the Provider against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or unlawful use of the Services.
watch_out.plain_english: The Customer has to defend the Provider in certain legal situations, which could lead to high costs for the Customer.
watch_out.why_flagged: This is a significant risk because it could lead to unexpected legal expenses for the Customer.
watch_out.suggested_negotiation: Customer shall defend Provider against third-party claims only to the extent arising from Customer's negligence or willful misconduct.

clause_balance.provider_terms: Provider is defended against claims related to Customer Data.
clause_balance.customer_terms: Customer must defend Provider against claims related to Customer Data.
clause_balance.asymmetry_summary: The Customer bears the burden of defense for claims related to its own data, while the Provider is shielded from such obligations.

evidence.quote: Customer shall defend Provider against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or Customer’s unlawful use of the Services, and shall pay damages finally awarded or settlements approved by Customer.

protections.title: Bilateral Confidentiality Obligations
protections.claim: The confidentiality obligations are bilateral and mutual, requiring each party to protect the other's confidential information.
protections.plain_english: Both parties must keep each other's confidential information safe, which is a good protection for the Customer.
protections.why_flagged: This matters because mutual confidentiality helps safeguard the Customer's sensitive information.
protections.suggested_negotiation: Add language to clarify that both parties are equally liable for breaches of confidentiality.

evidence.quote: Each Party shall protect the other Party’s Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and shall use such information only to perform or receive rights under this Agreement.

protections.title: Ownership of Data and Intellectual Property
protections.claim: Customer retains ownership of Customer Data, while Provider retains ownership of its own technology and services.
protections.plain_english: The Customer owns its data, while the Provider owns its technology, which is a good protection for the Customer.
protections.why_flagged: It's important for the Customer to know they retain ownership of their data, which protects them from potential misuse or loss of control.
protections.suggested_negotiation: Add a clause that specifies the Customer's rights to access, modify, and delete their data at any time.

clause_balance.provider_terms: Provider retains all right, title, and interest in the Services, software, models, templates, documentation, and Provider-developed technology.
clause_balance.customer_terms: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data.
clause_balance.asymmetry_summary: The Provider has broader rights over its technology compared to the Customer's rights over its data.

evidence.quote: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data. Provider retains all right, title, and interest in the Services, software, models, templates, documentation, and Provider-developed technology.

Subject to payment of all applicable fees, Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide license during the Term to use the Services for Customer’s internal business operations.

missing_clauses.title: Disaster Recovery SLA & RTO/RPO
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Without explicit Recovery Time / Recovery Point Objectives there is no contractual commitment for when service or data will be restored after a catastrophic outage.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan with a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of not more than 4 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of not more than 1 hour.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: No disaster recovery SLA or RTO/RPO targets found.

missing_clauses.title: Maximum Security Incident Notification Window
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Breach notification should have an hour-based maximum (e.g. 24-72 hours). Wording such as 'without undue delay' may cause the customer to miss regulatory reporting deadlines.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall notify Customer in writing without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours, after becoming aware of or confirming any Security Incident involving Customer Data.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Provider shall notify Customer without undue delay after confirming a Security Incident involving unauthorized access to Customer Data and shall provide reasonably available information concerning the nature and scope of the incident.

missing_clauses.title: Affirmative Data Deletion & Certification
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The provider should be obliged to return or destroy all customer data at the end of the contract and certify the destruction in writing.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Within thirty (30) days of termination, Provider shall, at Customer's election, return or permanently and securely destroy all Customer Data, and deliver written certification of compliance signed by an officer of Provider.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: No obligation to return or destroy customer data with written certification found.

missing_clauses.title: Advance Notice of New Subprocessors
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Subcontractors processing customer data should require advance notice and a right to object, otherwise compliance or data-residency policies may be breached without the customer knowing.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice before engaging any new subcontractor to process Customer Data, and Customer may object on reasonable security or compliance grounds.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Provider may use subcontractors to process Customer Data.

missing_clauses.title: Termination Right for Extended Force Majeure
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: If a force majeure event lasts a long time, the customer should be able to exit the contract instead of paying for services that cannot be delivered.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: If a Force Majeure event prevents performance of the Services for more than thirty (30) consecutive days, Customer may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice without penalty.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Neither Party shall be liable for delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, terrorism, government action, widespread internet failures, or labor disruptions, provided that…

missing_clauses.title: Customer Convenience Termination Parity
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: When only one side can walk away for convenience, or on much shorter notice, the other side carries the risk of a sudden exit.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Provider may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 15 days’ written notice to Customer. / Customer may terminate for convenience only after the first 12 months of the Term and upon 60 days’ written notice.

missing_clauses.title: Cyber Liability & E&O Insurance Commitments
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Technology Errors & Omissions and Cyber Liability insurance backstop the provider's indemnification and security commitments.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall maintain commercial general liability insurance, technology errors & omissions, and cyber liability insurance with policy limits of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence during the Term.

missing_clauses.title: Confidentiality Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: A confidentiality clause is a standard core protection for both parties.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Each Party shall protect the other Party's Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and use it only to perform this Agreement.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Each Party shall protect the other Party’s Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and shall use such information only to perform or receive rights under this Agreement.

missing_clauses.title: Limitation of Liability Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: A limitation of liability clause defines the maximum financial exposure of each party.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the fees paid or payable during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

missing_clauses.title: Termination Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: A termination clause defines how and when either party can end the agreement.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for material breach that remains uncured 30 days after written notice.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for material breach if the breach remains uncured for 30 days after written notice describing the breach.

risks.observation: The Standard tier overage rate (₹12 / document) is 140% higher than the Enterprise tier rate (₹5 / document). Usage spikes on a lower tier could cause unpredictable invoice increases.
risks.recommendation: Negotiate a monthly overage cap or an automatic tier upgrade when usage consistently exceeds the included quota.

risks.observation: Neither this pricing table nor the rest of the contract limits annual fee increases (e.g. a CPI link or a maximum percentage), so fees could rise on renewal.
risks.recommendation: Insert a price escalation cap: 'Fees shall not increase by more than 3% annually upon renewal.'

MASTER SOFTWARE SERVICES AND DATA
PROCESSING AGREEMENT
Agreement Date: 15 September 2026    Agreement ID: MSA-2026-0915-47
This Master Software Services and Data Processing Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by and between
Northstar Analytics Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under the laws of India, with its principal office at
Bengaluru, Karnataka (“Customer”), and Meridian Cloud Systems Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under the
laws of India, with its principal office at Hyderabad, Telangana (“Provider”). Customer and Provider are each a
“Party” and together the “Parties.”
1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 Confidential Information means non-public business, technical, financial, customer, security, product, pricing,
and operational information disclosed by either Party, whether marked confidential or whether a reasonable person
would understand the information to be confidential.
1.2 Customer Data means all information submitted to the Services by Customer or on Customer’s behalf,
including personal information, documents, source material, usage information, and audit records.
1.3 Services means the hosted analytics, document processing, reporting, API access, and related support
services described in this Agreement and its Schedules.
2. SERVICES AND SERVICE LEVELS
2.1 Provider shall provide the Services substantially in accordance with Schedule A. Provider may modify
non-material features from time to time, provided that such modification does not materially reduce the core
functionality of the Services.
2.2 Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly availability, excluding scheduled
maintenance, emergency maintenance, force majeure events, failures caused by Customer, and third-party
services outside Provider’s reasonable control.
2.3 Scheduled maintenance will normally be communicated at least 24 hours in advance. Emergency maintenance
may occur without prior notice where Provider reasonably believes that delay would create a security or
operational risk.
3. FEES AND PAYMENT

3.1 Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt. Undisputed late amounts may accrue interest at 1.5% per
month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower.
3.2 Provider may suspend access for invoices more than 15 days overdue after providing Customer with at least 7
days’ written notice and an opportunity to cure.
4. DATA PROCESSING AND SECURITY
4.1 Provider shall process Customer Data only to provide, secure, maintain, and improve the Services and to
comply with applicable law. Provider shall implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards

appropriate to the nature of the data processed.
4.2 Provider may use subcontractors to process Customer Data. Provider remains responsible for the acts and
omissions of its subcontractors to the same extent as if those acts or omissions were performed by Provider.
4.3 Provider shall notify Customer without undue delay after confirming a Security Incident involving unauthorized
access to Customer Data and shall provide reasonably available information concerning the nature and scope of
the incident.
4.4 Provider may retain backup copies of Customer Data for up to 180 days after deletion from production
systems, provided such copies remain protected and are not restored except for disaster recovery purposes.
5. CONFIDENTIALITY
5.1 Each Party shall protect the other Party’s Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and shall use
such information only to perform or receive rights under this Agreement.
5.2 The confidentiality obligations do not apply to information that the receiving Party can demonstrate was already
lawfully known, becomes public without breach, is independently developed, or is lawfully received from a third
party without a duty of confidentiality.
5.3 If disclosure is required by law, the receiving Party shall, where legally permitted, provide prompt notice and
reasonable cooperation so the disclosing Party may seek protective relief.
6. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
6.1 Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data. Provider retains all right, title, and interest in the
